add.issue.name: One expandable header per file diff, not a disclosure row stacked on pierre's

edit.description.md:
In a ticket's Commits tab an expanded file shows two headers: FileRow's own chevron+path button, and beneath it @pierre/diffs' sticky header (change dot, path again, +N/-N). Same name twice, one after the other.

Fold them into one: render our header through pierre's `renderCustomHeader` slot so the single header is the sticky one, carries the chevron, path, comment count, large-diff badge and stat, and toggles the file. Today a commit opens its files shut in the side pane and open in the full-width layout, with a remembered "Expand all"/"Collapse all" habit (YCT73R9) deciding the side pane. Reviewing means unfolding first every time the habit was last left shut.

add.issue.name: A "reviewed" checkbox per file diff, remembered in localStorage

edit.description.md:
Reviewing a ticket's commits file by file has nothing that says which ones are done. Put a "reviewed" checkbox in each file diff's header, like GitHub's Viewed.

- Checking collapses the file; unchecking opens it again.
- A reviewed file arrives collapsed when its commit is opened later, so the rest of the commit is what is left to read.
- Remembered per browser in localStorage, keyed by commit sha and path — a file reviewed in one commit says nothing about the same path in another.
- The checkbox sits outside the toggle button, so ticking it does not also fold or unfold the file by accident.

add.issue.name: The log splits into a column per actor, so who did what when is read across rather than down

edit.description.md:
A toggle in the log's header — beside Time / Actor / Type / Diff / Label — lays the log out as one lane per actor. Time still runs down the pane and each line keeps its place in it; what changes is that a line is indented into its actor's lane, so two agents working at once read as two streams rather than one interleaved list.

- Lanes come from the actors in the slice on screen, in first-appearance order, with a sticky heading row naming each in its own colour.

Built on branch `4CY51T3-log-actor-lanes`, not pushed — waiting on the user's look at it in the browser.

`lib/log-lanes.ts` owns who has a lane (actors in the slice, first appearance) and which lane a line is in; the layout is CSS on the pane, as the field columns are — a lane is an indent and a width per row, so splitting costs a custom property per line and no extra nodes. Two things the first pass got wrong and now hold: the heading row measured its lanes against a box narrowed by its own padding, so the names walked off their lanes; and the lane rules are drawn on a container whose `ch` differed from the rows', which put every rule ~15px off.

Open question for the review: lanes divide the pane evenly, so at panel width with four actors a label is cut after a few words. It reads well once the panel is dragged wide or popped out. A minimum lane width with a horizontal scroll is the alternative.

add.issue.name: The replay's spotlight on a moved card is cut off by the lane it sits in

edit.description.md:
While the history player runs, the card an event just landed on is flashed with a halo — a box-shadow spread growing 0 → 12px (`lib/theatre.ts:322`, `THEATRE_FLASH_FRAMES`, applied in `TicketCard.tsx:97`). The halo is clipped square at the lane's edge, so a card near the right of a column wears half a glow.

Two ancestors clip it:
- `SwimlaneColumn.tsx:321` — the card scroller is `overflow: auto` (the cards scroll vertically), which makes the horizontal axis clip too, and it has no side padding.
- `Panel.tsx:123` — the column panel is `overflow: hidden`, holding its own glow inside its corners.

Either give the scroller side padding the halo can bleed into and let the panel's clip start outside it, or draw the flash inside the card — an inset ring — so nothing has to overflow. The first keeps the look; the second is the cheaper change. Whichever is chosen, the card's own layout must not shift when the flash runs.

Solution: merged as PR #324 (rebase), commits `1aed9905` and `814b43f0`.

The panel toggles and the transport each sit in `fixtureWellStyle` — a panel2 ground, a hairline and 6px corners, 2px between the pair — so the two controls that are not about the chart, and that stay on the bar when the charts are shut, read as fixtures at either end. The row's `minHeight: 22` went with it; the wells make it 28 in both states, so the floor guarded nothing.

add.issue.name: Make the event log generic over its event map, so the core can be a package with more than one product on it

edit.description.md:
**Why.** The log machinery is a general substrate: per-actor append-only JSONL that git union-merges, order derived from `refId` + ULID, total replay, tombstones, pending log, state branch, contributor registry, time-travel cut. None of that is about boards. But today it is welded to board vocabulary: `AppEventMap` in `lib/event/event.model.ts` hard-codes ~25 board actions, and materialize, persist, load and boot mention issue/swimlane/board over a hundred times between them. A second product (a repo-persisted diagram app is the candidate) cannot consume it without forking.

**Scope.** Split `lib/event` into two halves with a one-way dependency:

- A generic core: id minting and the edge ref, the forest sort, dedupe, tombstoning by id, the pending log, persistence and load, the state branch, the contributor registry, `splitEventsAtTime`. Parameterised by an event map type and a reducer the product supplies. Owns every invariant in `.claude/skills/epiq-architecture` and ships with them as its contract.
- The board product: the current `AppEventMap`, its payload schemas, and the materialize reducer, moved out of the core and passed in.

**Out of scope.** Publishing the package, a monorepo, and the second product. This ticket only draws the boundary inside this repo, so that extraction later is a move rather than a rewrite.

**Done when.** `lib/event` core has no reference to issue, swimlane, board, tag or comment; `replay-equivalence.test.ts` and `npm run test:collab` are green; a reducer-only test constructs the log with a toy event map and no board code.

add.issue.name: Move the repo's commit and diff readers from mcp/ down into lib/

edit.description.md:
Prerequisite for the TUI diff view. Nothing user-visible.

`getCommitTimeline`, `getCommitsForRef`, `getCommitDiff`, `getSquashedDiffForRef` and `openCommitDiffInEditor` live in `source/mcp/epiq-time-travel.ts`, so today only the GUI websocket and MCP can reach them. The TUI is in `lib/`, and `lib/` must not import `mcp/` — the architecture puts `lib/` below it ("knows nothing about MCP, HTTP or React, which is what lets the same code answer all three"). There are currently **zero** `lib/` -> `mcp/` imports; `lib/` -> `git/` is routine (14 sites, incl. `lib/stats/repo-baseline.ts` already using `execGitAllowFail`/`readGitBlobsBatch`).

So move them down rather than import upwards. Their dependencies are already lib/git-only: `execGit`, `readGitBlobsBatch`, `getStateBranchRoot`, `resolveClosestEpiqProjectRoot`, `NODE_REF_LENGTH`, `Result`, `lib/editor`.

**Shape:** a new `source/lib/commits/` owning one concept — a repo's commits and their diffs.
- `commit-timeline.ts` — `CommitEntry`, `getCommitTimeline`, the 5s full-timeline cache, `getCommitsForRef`
- `commit-diff.ts` — `CommitDiffFile`, `getCommitDiff`, `getSquashedDiffForRef`
- `commit-editor.ts` — `openCommitDiffInEditor` and its VS Code side-by-side path

`resolveRepoRoot` and the `ToolInput` type move with them (both currently private to `epiq-time-travel.ts`).

**Pure move.** `epiq-time-travel.ts` re-exports, so no call site and no test import changes; the time-travel half (`checkoutStateAt`, `getEventTimeline`, `runExclusive`) stays where it is, since it does touch board and state.

Also unblocks `WF435EW` and `6YRCWTM`, which both want these readers shared across GUI/MCP/TUI from `lib/`.

add.issue.name: A Diff row on the TUI ticket: the commit list, and opening one in the editor

edit.description.md:
A ` Diff ›› ` row on the ticket detail, beside ` History ›› `, listing the commits whose subject carries this ticket's ref. `Enter` on one opens it in the configured editor.

Depends on `NV12WDB` (the readers must be reachable from `lib/` first).

**Why the editor hand-off is nearly free:** `openCommitDiffInEditor` already exists and already does VS Code side-by-side via `buildEditorDiffCommand`, falling back to a unified diff for other editors. It is wired only to the GUI today.

**Pieces:**
- `virtual-ids.ts` — a `'diff'` kind; `FieldNames.DIFF`
- `materializeTicketVirtualNodes` — rank `(MAX_RANK * 27n) / 32n`, placing it between History (13/16) and Comments (7/8)
- `TicketUI.tsx` — an `isInsideDiff` branch and a `renderNode` branch for the row
- `DiffListUI.tsx` — fetches on mount via `getCommitsForRef`, and attaches one nav node per commit the way `AttachmentListUI` does with `attachAttachmentNodes`, so arrow navigation and `Enter` work through the existing action map. `ScrollBoxUI` for the scrolling.

**The row carries no count**, unlike Comments and Attachments. Materialization is synchronous, runs for every ticket on every replay, and a commit count needs a git read — so the count appears once you are inside, not on the row. Do not reach for git in `materializeTicketVirtualNodes`.

TUI-only by construction: `setVirtualNodesEnabled(false)` in the GUI and MCP processes.

A new detail row shifts the arrow counts in the TUI e2e suite; update them with this.

add.issue.name: A unified diff pager in the TUI, coloured by +/- rather than by syntax

edit.description.md:
Read the diff without leaving the TUI. `Enter` on a commit in the ` Diff ›› ` list (`0XP205K`) opens a scrolling unified diff; the editor hand-off stays as the way out for a long read.

Depends on `0XP205K`.

**No syntax highlighting, deliberately.** `@pierre/diffs` is React-DOM and cannot render into ink, so nothing is reusable from the GUI's diff stack — the hunk rendering is ours either way. There is no terminal highlighter in `package.json`, so highlighting means a new dependency or a hand-rolled tokenizer, and at 80 columns added/removed/context/hunk-header colouring carries nearly all of the signal. If the colours are wanted, that is what opening in the editor is for. Revisit only if reading in the TUI actually proves hard.

Renders from `getCommitDiff`'s `before`/`after` strings, so the hunks are computed here rather than parsed out of `git diff` text.

Reuse `isLargeDiff`/`diffLineCount` from `lib/utils/diff-size.js` — the GUI already collapses a large file behind a "Show diff" prompt, and a lockfile is worse in a terminal, not better.

add.issue.name: Comment on a diff line from the TUI, additions side only

edit.description.md:
Write a line-anchored comment from the TUI's diff pager, landing as the same comment the GUI makes.

Depends on `882P3QD`.

**Most of this already exists.** The anchor is not a GUI concept: it is a marker in the comment body (`lib/utils/diff-comment.ts`), and `renderMarkdownLines` (`lib/utils/markdown-lite.ts:161`) already renders such a body in the TUI comment list as caption + numbered quoted lines. So the TUI already *reads* diff comments; only authoring is missing. No new event type — `add.issue.comment` with a body built by `encodeDiffCommentMarker`.

**Additions side only.** `diff-selection.ts:63-74` spells out why: an additions-side line number is a position in the new file that every view agrees on, whereas a deletions-side one is a position in whichever older file that view happened to diff against. `SquashedDiff.tsx:85` already filters to additions-only, so a deletions-anchored comment written here would render in the TUI and be silently dropped by the GUI's compacted view. Restrict the line cursor rather than writing an anchor the other surface cannot honour.

**Pieces:**

Deviation from the description on two points, both decided while implementing.

**It renders git's own patch, not hunks derived here.** The description said to render from `getCommitDiff`'s `before`/`after` strings and compute the hunks locally. That would have meant writing a diff algorithm to re-derive what git already computed, and then disagreeing with it about renames, binary blobs, mode-only changes and the missing trailing newline. So `getCommitPatch` runs `git show --no-ext-diff --no-color --patch --find-renames --format=` and `patch-parse.ts` reads the result. The `@@` headers also carry real line numbers, which is what `4X3TMF0` needs anyway.

A second consequence, in our favour: a patch is sized by what changed, not by how big the files are. The lockfile that defeats the GUI's blob-based `isLargeDiff` is usually a handful of rows here, so that check does not transfer — the cap is on patch rows instead, reusing `LARGE_DIFF_LINES`, because a nav node per row is what actually costs.

**Enter now reads; `o` opens the editor.** The description had Enter opening the pager but left the editor hand-off unplaced. `o` is a new `Intent.OpenInEditor`, and it works both from the commit list and from inside a patch. The list header changed from "enter to open in your editor" to "enter to read, o to open in your editor".

One judgement call worth recording: the gutter shows **new-revision line numbers only**, blank for a removed line. Numbering each row on its own side made the column read `1, 2, 3, 3, 5, 4` — two interleaved sequences looking like one broken one. The new-side number is also the only one that means the same thing in every view of that revision, which is what `4X3TMF0` will anchor to.

add.issue.name: Mark the lines that already carry a comment in the TUI diff pager

edit.description.md:
A line someone has already commented on looks identical to one nobody has read. The pager should say so in the margin.

Follows `4X3TMF0`, which made the comments; this is reading them back where they were made.

**Everything needed is already derived.** `nodeRepo.getCommentsByIssue(ticket.id)` gives the ticket's comments and `parseDiffCommentMeta` (`lib/utils/diff-comment.ts`) gives each one's `{sha, filePath, start, end, side}`. Nothing new is stored and no event changes.

**The rule:** a patch row is commented when a comment's `sha` is the open commit, its `filePath` is the row's file, and its additions-side range covers the row's new-revision line number. Exact matching on the same commit, so a line number always means what it says.

**Where it goes:** the space that currently sits between the line number and the `+`/`-` sign becomes the margin rule, so this costs no width — a `│` against the code, in the accent colour, the way a change bar reads in an editor.

**Deliberately not in scope**, both worth their own ticket if wanted:
- Comments made on a *different* commit that touched the same lines. Their line numbers are positions in that commit's revision, so placing them here means re-anchoring, which is the problem `SquashedDiff` solves in the GUI by only placing additions-side comments in the ticket's end state.
- Reading the comment without leaving the pager. The indicator says one is there; the Comments row is where it is read.

add.issue.name: fullscreen-lanes.pw.ts fails the pre-push gate under its own parallelism

edit.description.md:
`a wide fullscreen panel shows every pane side by side` (`source/test/e2e-gui/fullscreen-lanes.pw.ts:26`) times out after 30s on `page.getByTitle('Fullscreen').click()` during `git push`, and passes on its own.

Failed three consecutive gate runs while landing the TUI diff viewer, and passed every standalone `npx playwright test` (181/181) in between — which is what makes it read as a change having broken it when nothing had.

**Reproduced, so it is not a ghost.** `--repeat-each=6 --workers=6` on the file alone: 18/18 pass. The same file with the container suite running beside it (`EPIQ_SKIP_BUILD=1 npm run test:containers &`, then `--repeat-each=4`): **1 failure in 12**.

That is the gate's own shape. `source/scripts/pre-push.sh` runs lint, typecheck, the unit suite, the docker container suites and the whole browser suite *simultaneously* — deliberately, since nothing shares state. Under that load a 30s action timeout is not much headroom for a click that follows `setViewportSize(1600x900)` and a ticket creation.

Nothing here is specific to this test beyond it being the slowest; it is simply the one that runs out of headroom first. Adding e2e files makes it likelier, since the container stage grows.

- Give the browser stage its own timeout budget, or the gate fewer concurrent stages.

add.issue.comment.md:
Six review findings fixed on top of the original solution, in `019b24b2`, `f4087d50` and `3e9bc243`. Four were mine; two predate the branch.

**A patch line that begins like a path header.** A removed line reading `-- x` arrives as `--- x`, an added one reading `++ x` as `+++ x` — the same shape as the `---`/`+++` headers, which were matched before the "still in the header" guard. Read as headers they were dropped from the rows and stopped advancing the line numbers, so everything below was numbered one too low and a comment anchored there quoted the wrong code. Real in markdown rules, YAML separators and SQL comments. Pinned by a test, verified red.

**One terminal row per patch row.** A tab measures zero columns and renders four, so `truncateToWidth` passed tab-indented lines that then wrapped — every row two rows tall while `ScrollBoxUI` was told each was one, which is why the pager would not scroll to its own top. `expandTabs` plus `wrap="truncate-end"`. Also: `padTo` measured characters where `truncateToWidth` measured columns, so a CJK or emoji row overflowed the same way; and the header wrapped at 80 columns, stealing a row.

**A node per line was quadratic.** `createNode` derived the whole board per node and `deleteNode` copied the whole node map per node: 2.3s to open a 4000-line diff and 3.1s to leave. Now 6ms and 1ms, via `withDeferredDerive` and a new `nodeRepo.deleteNodes`. The event log's inline editor gets the same fix. Guarded by a test that fails on the quadratic shape.

**The pager is now recognised by the patch it has open**, not by a parent field whose title a ticket could also carry. A ticket literally named "Diff" would otherwise have had its comments read for a line anchor.

**Predating this branch:** `nodes.text` accepted a `props` argument and always wrote `props: {}`, which silently disabled the command palette's own "unavailable" guard (`palette-actions.ts:66` reads `props.disabled`). Confirmed dead on `main` too. Replaced with a `disabled` flag — it could not simply be honoured, because every node's `props.value` is swept into the autocomplete corpus, which would have put every line of an open diff into the vocabulary.

**Also:** `o`/`s`/`c` were advertised in the shortcut bar on every screen, displacing real hints, while answering "nothing to do that to here" everywhere but the diff. Descriptions dropped; the commit list and pager name them in their own headers.

And from the user: enter on a line now opens `:comment lines:4-9 `, so the range is visible and editable in the command line instead of held in invisible state — which deleted that state.
